newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Savage groups bids for Peru's Mahr Tunel.
newsitem.headline: Savage groups bids for Peru's Mahr Tunel.

text.p: Savage Resources Ltd said on Tuesday that it and joint venture partner Simsa, an affiliate of Phelps Dodge Corp, had bid for the Peruvian government's Mahr Tunel base metals mining complex.
The company said the bid, with a minimum bid price of US$50 million set by Peru's state mining company Centromin, was lodged in the Peruvian capital of Lima on July 14.
It said the bid was one of three under an international tender process. The other bids were lodged by Canada's Boliden Inc, a unit of Boliden AB of Sweden, and Compania Minera Volcan SA of Peru.

Savage said its joint venture partner Simsa was Peru's third largest private sector mining company and 40 percent of its voting shares were held by Phelps Dodge of the United States which had helped develop the bid.

"Financing offers have been received for the debt portion for this initiative and Savage's equity requirements are available from existing cash reserves," the company said without specifying how much it had bid for the project.
It said the successful bidder would be named in Lima on July 18.
Mahr Tunel controls the San Cristobal and Andaychagua mines, which lie close to each other in the central Peruvian highlands.
In 1996, San Cristobal produced 680,000 dry tonnes of ore containing zinc, lead, copper and silver while Andaychagua produced about 395,000 dry tonnes of ore with silver, lead and zinc.
